properties.source: Derived: the convex hull of this port's terminals and way 972535620 from OpenStreetMap, grown by 500 m, then cut to the water OpenStreetMap maps inside it (the sea within its coastline, rivers, docks and basins), with the terminals and those areas kept whole
properties.disjoint: The customs and agriculture border inspection post behind the berths is kept whole, and OpenStreetMap's water does not join it to the harbour, so it is a part of its own.
properties.note: OpenStreetMap maps no port limits for Rosslare. These are the hull of the four berths and the customs and agriculture border inspection post behind them (tagged industrial=port), grown by 500 m, then cut to the water OpenStreetMap maps inside it, with the terminals and those areas kept whole and a 30 m margin where they meet the water. A scan of OpenStreetMap finds no homes, residential land, schools, hospitals, places of worship or named places inside.

properties.name: Berth 1
properties.note: Berths 1 to 4, each tagged waterway=dock with no cargo tag. Ro-ro and passenger are from the ferry routes OpenStreetMap maps from Rosslare (Stena Line, Irish Ferries, Brittany Ferries, DFDS), whose ships carry freight and passengers. The name Rosslare Europort is from its public transport stop.
